patterns.usage_note: Knocks down what the listener was assuming and puts the contrary state of affairs in its place: the first item is denied, not topped. The second clause typically carries a negative, かえって, or も to mark how far reality falls the other way; when instead it names something that outdoes the first item ('バイクどころか車まで持っている'), that is the additive どころか of the ダケデナク family. It attaches straight to a bare noun with no particle, to the bare stem of a な-adjective (元気どころか、寝込んでいる), and to the plain form of verbs and い-adjectives. どころではない states that circumstances rule X out; どころか needs a second clause that overturns or outdoes X.

examples.ruby: あいつは反省[はんせい]どころか、こっちに文句[もんく]を言[い]ってきた。
examples.english: Sorry? Far from it, he turned around and complained at me.

examples.ruby: 今月[こんげつ]は旅行[りょこう]どころか、外食[がいしょく]する余裕[よゆう]もない。
examples.english: Forget a trip this month, I can't even afford to eat out.

examples.ruby: この薬[くすり]は効[き]くどころか、かえって熱[ねつ]が上[あ]がった。
examples.english: Far from helping, this medicine actually pushed my fever higher.
